title: Lowlight release sequencer notes
content:
Context:
This is my working notebook for the next low‑impact rollout (we're calling it 'lowlight' because it should be quiet) — objective is to flip a runtime change + model variant with minimal churn and predictable economics. High level: staged tenant sequencing, per‑tenant version pin map, explicit warmup windows with synthetic priming and a small steady cohort that carries KV cache state.

Goals / success criteria:
- No more than 0.1% error rate delta vs baseline during 95% of rollout windows.
- Latency P95 change <= 30ms for production traffic slices we care about.
- Model/runtime fallbacks engage automatically with no more than 2m of client-facing increased latency.
- Can pin back to previous runtime/model within 2 minutes for any tenant.

Non‑goals:
- Broad load tests in this window (these are scheduled separately).
- Full quantization rollouts — this is a small optimization and routing change only.

Phased plan (sequencer):
Phase 0 — preflight (T-48 to T-2 hours)
- Sanity checks: infra health, disk pressure, GPU memory headroom.
- Snapshot current pin map to S3 / release record.
- Run smoke on staging with representative token sequences (long tail tokens included).
- Verify observability dashboards readable and templated (labels: release=lowlight, cohort=warmup).
- Notify channels: #deploys + oncall.

Phase 1 — quiet warmup cohort (T0 to T0+3h)
- Direct 0.05% of production RPS (weighted across regions) to new runtime/model variant. Prefer tenants that already exercise the hot path (embedding-heavy tenants are poor choices here).
- Warmup objective: build KV caches and check prefix caching behavior for common prefixes.
- Duration: at least 3 hours or until key warmup metrics stabilize: cache hit ratio within 10% of expected, average decode latency stable 
- Monitoring: alert if errors > 0.5% or p95 increase > 50ms.

Phase 2 — anchored tenant sequencing (T0+3h to T0+12h)
- Add 3 more tenant cohorts (0.2%, 0.5%, 1% respectively) incrementally, waiting 30–60 minutes between steps if signals are stable.
- For each tenant cohort: ensure per‑tenant pin map updated and stored in release record (TenantA->runtime:1.12.3, model:open-llama-3-small-q8).
- Observability: per‑tenant traces + token-level cost delta.

Phase 3 — broader drip (T0+12h to T0+48h)
- Expand traffic to 5% then 20% with 2x hold windows (1–2 hours) to catch diurnal variance.
- Continue to sequence new tenants by affinity: free users -> paid -> enterprise with canary toggles for enterprise.
- Keep a shadow or mirrored path for critical enterprise tenants until 20% complete.

Phase 4 — ramp to steady (T0+48h to T0+7d)
- Increase to 50% for 24h, watch long‑tail regressions (rare prompt combos).
- If stable, move to 100% over a weekend low traffic window.

Traffic shaping & tenant selection heuristics:
- Prefer tenants with frequent short prompts (helps warm cache quickly).
- Avoid tenants with heavy streaming / function-calling until after 20% stable.
- Enterprise tenants must be opt‑in unless explicitly requested; add them last.
- Keep a 1% steady control cohort on old runtime for A/B signal.

Version pinning / rollback map:
- Every tenant update must be recorded in release_record.csv (S3 path). Columns: timestamp, tenant_id, old_runtime, new_runtime, old_model, new_model, operator, reason.
- Quick rollback: attach an automated job that flips tenant routing in the sequencer via API with "rollback":true flag. Target flip completion within 120 seconds.
- Post‑rollback verification: run smoke on the tenant quotas and check KV cache miss spikes.

Warmup scripts and primers (operational snippets):
- Synthetic priming: fire 500 short prompts per tenant within 10 minutes to prepopulate KV caches (script: tools/primers/short-priming.sh).
- Long tail probe: 50 longer multimodal-ish sequences to ensure attention window behavior is correct.
- Quiet traffic generator: replay 5% of last 24h sampled requests in read-only mode to a mirror cluster for second-order checks.

Observability & signals (what I will watch live):
- Error budget and HTTP 5xx / 4xx by tenant (alert above thresholds).
- Per‑tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, tokenization errors, decode stalls.
- Cache hit ratio and KV eviction rates — sudden drop may indicate cold paths not being warmed.
- Cost-per-token and median token compute time (to catch cost regressions).
- Semantic quality smoke: run a small eval set (50 prompts) every 30 minutes and track quality score delta.

Rollback criteria (immediate rollback if any of):
- A sustained increase in error rate above 1% for > 10 minutes for > 3 tenants.
- p95 latency regression > 200ms for core production routes for 5 continuous minutes.
- Any reproducible correctness regression on the eval set (quality delta > 0.15) that correlates with rollout.
- Unexpected memory OOMs on runtime hosts.

Escalation flow:
- Pager: oncall SRE alerted via pagerduty -> if not acked within 2 minutes, escalate to eng-serving-runtime lead.
- Quick triage: is this config/routing? If yes, flip sequencer back and isolate region.
- If code/pathological performance, engage release owner and standby runtime dev.

Post rollout tasks:
- Reconcile release_record.csv and update CHANGELOG (include tenant list + timing).
- Run full regression eval (2k prompts) and surface quality drift.
- Capacity accounting: update cost delta dashboard and estimate net delta per million tokens.
- Retrospective doc: collect signals, what we learned, and recommended guardrails.

Open questions / TODOs (my immediate actionable list):
- [ ] Add small automated test that checks prefix caching for the most common 20 prefixes (ticket: ENG-4189).
- [ ] Confirm priming script runs in all regions (cc @Ethan).
- [ ] Add a tenant metadata flag to prefer warmup (e.g., warmup_preference:high).
- [ ] Hook the sequencer flip API into a fast rollback endpoint and test it end‑to‑end in staging.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep quiet windows in local region when flipping enterprise tenants so customer success can join.
- If we see small oscillations early, do a slow-drip instead of full pause — often oscillations self-correct after cache warms.
- Document the probe prompts used in the eval set; they should represent edge cases.

Last checked: incremental sanity OK on staging (2025-01-28). Next action: schedule T-48 preflight and loop in Maya for tenant sequencing list (I will assemble initial 12 tenants and annotate reasons).
